findings.title: Default-strategy tests do not enable rolling-updates feature
findings.body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before setting FeatureSpec.enabledFeatures to rolling-updates at lines 112-115. Both parameterized tests use the null case: testCacheMaxCount with null expects a rolling upgrade and testImageChange with null expects the operator to determine a recreate upgrade. With the new gating, the update-compatibility commands exit with FEATURE_DISABLED when rolling-updates is not enabled, so the null-strategy cases no longer exercise the intended default upgrade-decision path and will either fail or pass for the wrong (feature-disabled) reason. The feature must be enabled for every deployment created here, regardless of whether an explicit update strategy is set.

findings.title: Feature-disabled exit code and check subcommand are untested
findings.body: The new testFeatureNotEnabled only launches the metadata subcommand and only asserts the stderr message; it does not assert the new exit code 4 (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) and does not cover UpdateCompatibilityCheck, which has its own duplicated feature-gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run(). A regression that prints the message but exits 0, or that breaks the gate in the check subcommand only (the subcommand whose exit code is documented for scripting in update-compatibility.adoc), would not be caught. Add a check-subcommand case and assert exit code 4 for both subcommands.
